title: Federal Budget & NDAA Weekly Tracker
description: Fiscal 2027 appropriations, the continuing resolution, NDAA status, reconciliation funds and Golden Dome money.
readFirst: Little floor action this week. Congress is out until after the Nov. 3 election. The continuing resolution still runs through Dec. 11. The new item is The Hill's Oct. 19 account of lame-duck leverage on the defense bills. Golden Dome's fiscal 2027 request is unchanged: almost all of it is in reconciliation that has not passed.

items.headline: A continuing resolution funds the government through December 11 and holds up new starts
items.summary: The Congressional Research Service overview of Division A of P.L. 119-103 says the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 funds agencies covered by all 12 regular bills from Oct. 1 through Dec. 11, 2026. The bill text continues fiscal 2026 rates and, for the Department of Defense, bars those funds from new production of items not funded for production in fiscal 2026 or earlier and from raising production rates above the fiscal 2026 level. The same section restricts starting or resuming a project that did not already have appropriations authority. Breaking Defense reported in October that more than 150 new military programs face delay under that CR, and that another CR or a funding gap is still possible when Dec. 11 arrives. No full-year defense appropriation was enacted in the Oct. 14–22 window.

items.headline: The Hill: regular defense funding and a June emergency request are the lame-duck holdup
items.summary: The Hill reported Oct. 19 that Senate Democrats are threatening to hold up emergency defense funding the White House requested in June, and the regular Defense funding that expires Dec. 11, unless the Iran war is wrapped up. Sen. Brian Schatz said that if the war is over there is a path to bipartisan work on defense appropriations, and that if it is not, a deal will be extremely difficult. These are positions The Hill attributed to senators before the chamber left for the Nov. 3 election. No full-year bill moved in the Oct. 14–22 window.

items.headline: The Hill: the NDAA is tied up in the same post-election leadership fight
items.summary: The same Oct. 19 report says Democrats have floated Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's departure after the Nov. 3 election as a condition for cooperation on defense measures in the lame duck, and that some Republican sources see a possible leadership change. Sen. Tim Kaine told The Hill a resignation could lower the temperature on the NDAA and the defense appropriations bill. The Hill also reported Democrats are threatening to hold up a waiver for Hung Cao, the Navy secretary nominee, who needs one because of the waiting period for former officers. None of this is an enacted condition. It is the state of the authorization talks while both chambers are out.

items.headline: Golden Dome's fiscal 2027 money is still a reconciliation problem
items.summary: CSIS's budget tracker says the department requested $17.1 billion of a $17.9 billion Golden Dome total in the reconciliation package, not in discretionary appropriations, and that the program manager has warned a lack of fiscal 2027 funding would prevent further development. Axios reported Oct. 7 that senators questioned feasibility and cost after a Sept. 29 hearing, with the Congressional Budget Office's 20-year estimate as high as $1.2 trillion against Gen. Michael Guetlein's $185 billion figure. No reconciliation vehicle clearing that request was found in the Oct. 14–22 window.
